title: SEND Services: Joint Commissioning Statutory Requirement

contributions.text: 8. What discussions she has had with Cabinet colleagues on introducing a statutory requirement for local authorities and integrated care boards to jointly commission SEND services.
contributions.name: David Williams

contributions.who: The Minister for School Standards (Georgia Gould)
contributions.text: Joint commissioning between local authorities and integrated care boards is key to the successful delivery of special educational needs and disabilities services. I recently met the Minister for Social Care and Mental Health to discuss strengthening the role of health partners across the SEND system, and we are committed to achieving that.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: It is so important that partners jointly commission services such as speech and language therapy. However, despite the requirements set out in the Children and Families Act 2014, families tell me that joint commissioning is often inconsistent and insufficient to meet need, and that they often feel like they are being passed from pillar to post. Will the Minister therefore introduce a stronger statutory requirement for local areas to jointly commission services for young people with SEND issues across universal, targeted and specialist layers of support?
contributions.name: David Williams

contributions.text: My hon. Friend is right: it is essential that we have greater integration between health, social care and education. That is why we are putting £1.8 billion into Experts at Hand. That is about the joint commissioning of speech and language therapists, educational psychologists, occupational therapists and other specialist support, but he is absolutely right that we need to strengthen joint commissioning, and we will set out more on that in due course.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: Like the constituents of the hon. Member for Stoke-on-Trent North (David Williams), Guildford families tell me that their children with SEND can end up with fragmented care, and that parents are left with no co-ordination between health and education. As the Surrey SEND reforms are implemented, and the new West Surrey council prepares to take on responsibilities following the local government reorganisation, how will the Government ensure that joint commissioning leads to earlier support and better outcomes for children, with clear accountability when those outcomes are not achieved?
contributions.name: Zöe Franklin

contributions.text: That is exactly why we are putting the new investment into the system, including £4 billion into early intervention. Through the SEND reform plans, we are asking ICBs and local authorities to come together with clear plans for implementation. In the new system, we are proposing national inclusion standards that set out really clearly our expectations on early intervention, and new duties for schools to recognise need and put in place individual support plans. It is so important that we are wrapping that wider support around schools. Families should not have to fight for it; it should just be available.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould
